summary: Config: reads one named parameter from the cloud service's config and outputs its value.
description: DbConfig (Config) fetches the cloud service's config once when the node initializes and outputs the value of the parameter chosen with the `configKey` (Parameter) input — server-managed settings like feature flags, welcome texts or API keys, edited on the cloud service rather than baked into the app. The `value` output is typed from the config schema (string, boolean, number, object or array). A Local Override group (`useDevValue` Enable + `devValue` Value) lets you substitute a local value, but only while running locally with the editor connected — deployed apps always read the real config.
whenToUse: Use it whenever behaviour or copy should be changeable on the server without redeploying the app. It is read-only and fetched once at startup; for per-record data use DbCollection2 / DbModel2, and for values the app computes itself use Variable or Object nodes.
runtimeBehavior: All ports are runtime-determined from the project's cloud config schema (`dbConfigSchema` metadata): `configKey` is registered as an edit-only enum of the parameter names (master-key-only parameters are listed only in cloud functions), the `value` output takes the selected parameter's type, and the Local Override inputs (`useDevValue`, then `devValue` when enabled) appear for basic types. An authoring tool should set `configKey` in parameters and read the `value` output; the editor warns if the key does not exist in the schema.

ports.value: Value output with the selected config parameter; typed from the config schema, updates once the config has loaded (and when a local override changes).

patterns: `value` → a Text's `text`: server-editable copy such as banners or announcement messages.
`value` (boolean parameter) → a Group's `visible` or a Button's `enabled`: feature flags without redeploying.
